newsitem.title: USA: NY police officer killed in shootout.
newsitem.headline: NY police officer killed in shootout.

text.p: A New York police lieutenant was fatally shot on Friday night during a wild shootout with a gunman who was later slain by other police officers, city officials said.

The gunman, who was said to have a lengthy criminal record, was killed in the lobby of a nearby apartment building in the Flatbush section of Brooklyn after the man fired a hail of bullets at pursuing police.
"The family is going through torture right now," an angry and upset Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said outside Kings County Hospital in Brooklyn where the officer died.
"This is one that did not have to happen if we had a rational and sensible criminal justice system," he said.

Police said the gunman, Harvey Richardson, 65, in trouble with the law since 1957, had a criminal record that stretched six feet (1.8 metres) for such crimes as felonies, assaults on police officers and attempted murder.
The officer, Federico Narvaez, had been on the force since 1979 and leaves a wife and small child.
According to witnesses, shortly after 7 p.m., a woman, apparently being stalked by the alleged gunman, flagged down a passing patrol car seeking help.

When the lieutenant called out to Richardson, he is said to have pulled out a gun and shot the officer in the face. Other officers coming to the lieutenant's assistance, chased the gunman to a building where shots were exchanged.
